turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor Pillay, I've got Mr Naidoo in the room. The dressing is still on the hernia wound; I waited for you before taking it down.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, Sister Jacobs. Mr Naidoo, I'm Doctor Pillay. What's been worrying you?

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. It is ten days since the hernia operation on the right side, and the wound has become rather red, with some discharge, so I thought it best to come in.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been fretting since Wednesday, Doctor. The redness started three days ago, and there's been quite a lot of ooze on the dressing every time I've looked.

[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Forgive me, my dear, that is not quite so. I noticed the redness only yesterday, or perhaps the evening before, and the discharge is a small amount, not a great quantity.

[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me make sure I have this. The repair was ten days ago, you noticed a little redness and discharge about yesterday, and your wife recalls three days with more ooze, so I'll keep both in mind. Any fever with it?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. Last night I felt properly feverish, hot and then rather cold, though this morning it seems to have eased.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was burning up. Our thermometer at home read thirty-eight point six, and he shivered for hours. I hardly slept myself.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Well, actually, the shivering was about an hour, not the entire night. I would not wish to overstate it.

[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. A home reading of thirty-eight point six, rigors for roughly an hour by your own account, and you feel a little better now. Sister, what did you record this morning?
[SEG0011] person_1 (NURSE): Temp is thirty-seven point eight, pulse 96, blood pressure 138 over 82. Sats 97 percent on room air, and his respiratory rate is 16. He walked in without any trouble.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is the wound painful?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): It is sore, Doctor, a dull ache. It is worse if I stand or if I cough, and if I keep still it is tolerable.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor, no vomiting.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any diarrhoea, or stinging when you pass urine?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Neither, thank you. I have passed water normally, and the bowels opened yesterday without difficulty.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any shortness of breath?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): The robot on Voortrekker Road was out, I'm afraid, and there was a dreadful queue of bakkies. We were a little late, and I do apologise.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's quite all right. Coming back to what I asked — any shortness of breath, or pain in the chest?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): I beg your pardon, Doctor. No shortness of breath, and no chest pain.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): After the operation, were you given an antibiotic?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. It was Augmentin, the amoxicillin with clavulanic acid, one tablet twice a day. I took it for five days... or was it seven? I am not entirely sure.
[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The discharge summary from the hospital said seven days. He finished the box, I think — no, wait, he missed one dose the afternoon we were stuck at the chemist.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, I may have missed that single dose. I am sorry I cannot be more precise about the days.

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll summarise that. Augmentin, one tablet twice a day, for somewhere between five and seven days, course now finished, and possibly one dose missed. Do you remember the strength of the tablet?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): I believe it was six hundred and twenty-five milligrams. The box is at home, unfortunately.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll note six hundred and twenty-five milligrams, though we haven't seen the box. Do you take anything else regularly?

[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Panado, one gram, up to three times a day since the operation, for the pain. And amlodipine, five milligrams each morning, for my blood pressure, which I have had for years.

[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): So paracetamol one gram up to three times daily, and amlodipine five milligrams every morning for longstanding hypertension. Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): None that I know of, Doctor.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): No known allergies, then. Sister, would you take the dressing down and tell us what you see?

[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): Dressing's off. There's yellow-green discharge on the gauze, not a huge amount, and the skin is red and warm for about four centimetres either side. The stitches are still in, and I don't see the wound pulling open.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. I'll have a look myself, Mr Naidoo, and it may be a bit tender.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Of course, Doctor. Please go ahead.

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): The wound is red and tender, with a small amount of pus at the lower end. I can't feel a collection underneath, and the repair itself feels intact. Your abdomen is soft, and it isn't tender once I come away from the wound.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): That is a relief, about the repair. Thank you.
[SEG0038] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was exhausted yesterday, Doctor. He slept the whole afternoon, and he hardly touched his food.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): I was a little tired, that is true, but I did manage soup and some bread in the evening. I would not say I hardly ate.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mild tiredness, which you confirm, and you did eat something, so I'll not call it a poor intake. Any rash elsewhere, or pain in the calves?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): No rash, Doctor, and my legs are quite all right.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a superficial infection of the hernia wound. That is provisional only; I wouldn't call it confirmed until we see what grows, if anything.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): I understand, Doctor.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like a wound swab sent today. The Augmentin course is already finished and the wound has still flared, so I'll change you to flucloxacillin, five hundred milligrams, four times a day, by mouth, for seven days.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): Four times a day. I shall set an alarm, so that I do not miss any this time.
[SEG0046] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should the wound stay covered?

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Sister will put a clean dry dressing on. Keep it clean and dry, don't soak in the bath, and wash your hands before you touch it. If the redness spreads quickly, or the fever climbs over 38.5 again, or the discharge becomes much heavier, come back sooner or go to casualty.
[SEG0048] person_1 (NURSE): I'll swab it now, before I put the new dressing on, if that's all right.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please do. Label it as a right inguinal hernia wound swab, query infection.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): Will the stitches come out today, Doctor?
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today. With the infection I'd rather leave them, and see you again in three days here in clinic, to check the wound and the swab result if it is back.
[SEG0052] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three days. We'll book it at reception on the way out.
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. A neighbour of mine was back at his desk a week after his own hernia, though I suppose that is neither here nor there.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): People mend at different speeds, so I wouldn't measure yourself against him. Was there anything else you wanted to ask?
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. You have explained it most clearly. Thank you kindly.
[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): Right, we'll do the swab, and then I'll walk you both to the desk.
